notes: Historical financials (revenue, EBIT, D&A, capex) are taken from Generac’s FY2025 Form 10-K; amounts in the filing are reported in thousands of USD and were scaled to full USD units. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926004568/gnrc20251231_10k.htm))

Historical NWC is computed as: NWC = (Total current assets - Cash and cash equivalents) - (Total current liabilities - Short-term borrowings - Current portion of long-term borrowings and finance lease obligations). This excludes interest-bearing debt from working capital. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926004568/gnrc20251231_10k.htm))

Base-case forecast drivers are modeling assumptions: revenue growth and profitability are anchored to FY2026 guidance (mid-teens) with a taper; D&A%, capex%, and NWC% are normalized toward multi-year historical averages with mild evolution. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926003700/ex_919348.htm))

Tax_rate is set to 0.19 based on FY2025 effective tax rate (GAAP provision / pre-tax income). WACC (0.095) and terminal_growth (0.025) are DCF assumptions, not explicitly provided in filings. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926004568/gnrc20251231_10k.htm))

NOL balance uses the disclosed 'tax loss carryforwards of approximately $197,981' from the income tax note; NOL utilization is an assumption (0.80) because the filing does not provide a year-by-year utilization schedule tied to the DCF. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926004568/gnrc20251231_10k.htm))

Investments are modeled as the average non-capex investing cash outflows: purchase of long-term investments + acquisition of businesses (net of cash acquired) + other investing activities; capex is excluded because it is modeled separately. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926004568/gnrc20251231_10k.htm))
Comps: NTM EV/Revenue, EV/EBITDA, and NTM P/E were left null due to missing retrieval of NTM-specific valuation multiples from a primary market data source in this run.

catalysts: Data center and C&I order momentum translating into higher shipped volumes and backlog conversion during 2026–2027. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926003700/ex_919348.htm))

GAAP margin recovery as abnormal/one-time items fade and operating leverage improves with higher sales volumes. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926003700/ex_919348.htm))
Additional capacity/capex execution supporting product availability for C&I and outage-driven residential demand.
company_overview: Generac designs and manufactures power generation equipment and energy technology solutions for residential and commercial markets, including data centers. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926003700/ex_919348.htm))

Management reports net sales across residential products and commercial & industrial (C&I) products, with growth influenced by outage environment and customer-driven install demand. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926004568/gnrc20251231_10k.htm))

The company maintains a financing structure supported by revolver/term loan facilities and uses cash flow for capex and buybacks. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926004568/gnrc20251231_10k.htm))
current_context: FY2025 net sales were $4.21 billion (down 2% vs. 2024) and net income was $161.4 million; management highlighted weaker residential/outage conditions and higher operating costs including legal/regulatory items. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926003700/ex_919348.htm))

For FY2026, management initiated guidance for mid-teens consolidated net sales growth; residential product sales expected to rise ~10% and C&I product sales expected to increase in the ~30% range. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926003700/ex_919348.htm))

FY2026 profitability expectations include net income margin of ~0.08–0.09 (before noncontrolling interests), with adjusted EBITDA margin of ~0.18–0.19. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926003700/ex_919348.htm))
Market pricing as of the latest trade prior to 2026-03-21 is approximately $199.31 per share.
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth reflects management’s mid-teens FY2026 outlook and a taper to more normalized mid-to-high single-digit growth through 2030. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926003700/ex_919348.htm))

EBIT margin improves from the FY2025 GAAP level as the model assumes normalization of cost pressures and a recovery toward management’s longer-run profitability profile. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926003700/ex_919348.htm))

Capital intensity is modeled as easing from FY2025’s elevated capex level toward a steadier run-rate, consistent with a growth-and-capacity investment cycle. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926004568/gnrc20251231_10k.htm))

Working-capital intensity is modeled to remain meaningfully positive but gradually normalize from the historical range as forecasting moves away from specific-year working capital swings. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926004568/gnrc20251231_10k.htm))
key_risks: Residential demand sensitivity to the outage environment could pressure volumes and margins versus the modeled rebound. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926003700/ex_919348.htm))

Legal/regulatory outcomes and other non-recurring items may continue to distort GAAP operating profit and cash conversion. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926003700/ex_919348.htm))
Working capital volatility could affect free cash flow and reinvestment capacity in any given year.

valuation_summary: DCF base case is anchored on a 2025 GAAP baseline, then overlays management’s FY2026 growth and a conservative taper to terminal-era economics using gordon_growth with 0.025 terminal growth. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926003700/ex_919348.htm))
A separate comps framework is included, but NTM-specific EV/Revenue and EV/EBITDA inputs were not fully retrieved from a single primary market-multiples source in this run (placeholders are null).

Net debt and tax attributes are incorporated at model setup using year-end cash/debt and disclosed tax loss carryforwards; NOL utilization is treated as an assumption due to limited disclosed utilization mechanics. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001474735/000143774926004568/gnrc20251231_10k.htm))
